rationale: The open-label original treats cancer-related constipation with elobixibat. Oral food intake is a stratifier. Pain relates to opioid use or adverse events. No dried date-fruit comparison is described.
The standardized high-fat meal used medication pharmacokinetics, with reported back and puncture-site pain as adverse events. The ingredient list contains no date fruit.

The videoconference study assesses broad nutritional status in older adults. Pain is a Nottingham Health Profile domain. There is no assessment of dried date-fruit intake or an ingredient-specific pain estimate.
The cross-sectional study measures nocturnal urine output under tube-feeding practices. Low-back pain appears in background and no dried date-fruit exposure is described.

The PRIME protocol gives broad fruit and personalized menu guidance for a combined diet and exercise program. Its pain mentions concern adverse-event monitoring. The published methods do not specify dried dates or a date-fruit pain comparison.
The original fed-fasted crossover tests drug exposure under a standardized high-fat meal. Oropharyngeal pain appears in an adverse-event table and there is no identified date-fruit exposure.

The NutriAct protocol names barley and barley flakes as usual-care foods and plans GAD-7. Parkinson disease is an exclusion example. The trial does not allocate boiled barley separately and the protocol contains no outcome results.
The olive-oil passage describes the Mediterranean diet pattern. This review provides no separately measured cold-pressed olive oil and postural instability severity contrast.
The antinociceptive section is about lemon balm, including its extract and oil. It provides no fresh sage comparison.

Both soup mixtures contained 5 g parsley per 100 g. They differed from the control in many foods and diet components. Fecal mass was higher in both mixtures. Fresh parsley, Parkinson disease and clinical constipation severity were not isolated.
Insomnia outcomes in the reviewed reports refer to lemon balm. The article gives no dried sage and Parkinson insomnia comparison.

Both powders contain 5 g olive oil per 100 g, with oil grade unspecified. Both mixtures had higher fecal mass than the control. The multi-ingredient rat comparison does not isolate extra-virgin olive oil.
